pick.name: Docker Desktop
pick.what: Docker Engine + Compose + GUI on all three OSes
pick.why: Most polished, identical workflow everywhere, widest tool compatibility
pick.free_limits: Free for personal use, education, non-commercial open source, and commercial undertakings with fewer than 250 employees AND under US$10M annual revenue; government entities must pay. Paid: Pro $9/user/mo annual ($11 monthly), Team $15 ($16), Business $24 annual
pick.install: brew install --cask docker | winget install Docker.DockerDesktop

best_free.name: Podman Desktop
best_free.why: Fully free OSS licence with no revenue threshold
best_free.install: brew install podman-desktop | winget install RedHat.Podman-Desktop

alts.name: OrbStack
alts.what: Fast lightweight Docker/Linux VM runtime for macOS
alts.free_limits: Free for personal, non-commercial use only; commercial Pro $8/user/month

alts.name: Docker Engine (CE)
alts.why: Native on Linux; inside WSL2 on Windows; no licence test

candidates.name: Podman Desktop
candidates.verdict: best free; compose parity mostly fine, not verified

candidates.name: OrbStack
candidates.verdict: best on macOS; commercial needs paid plan

decision: Docker Desktop is the smoothest cross-platform choice and is free for companies under 250 employees and US$10M revenue; above that, or for government use, a paid seat (Pro, Team or Business) is required. Pick OrbStack on macOS (Pro $8/user/mo for commercial use), Docker Engine on Linux, and Podman Desktop when you want a licence-free GUI.
details: Docker Desktop and OrbStack terms read from official pages on 2026-10-28; verify current terms before relying on them.

os_notes.macOS: OrbStack is fastest but commercial use needs Pro ($8/user/mo); Docker Desktop or Colima/Podman as alternatives.
os_notes.Windows: Docker Desktop (WSL2 backend) or Docker Engine CE inside WSL2 for no licence test.
os_notes.Linux: Install Docker Engine CE from the official repo; Docker Desktop for Linux exists but is rarely needed.

verify.note: Licence s.4.2 quoted on the FAQ; 'and' means both thresholds apply.
